claims.text: Dose: 6 mg rapid IV bolus over 1–2 s,
claims.quote: Initial dose : 6 mg given as a rapid intravenous bolus (administered over a 1 to 2 second period).

claims.text: given as close to the pt as poss and followed by a rapid saline flush;
claims.quote: it should be given as close to the patient as possible and followed by a rapid saline flush.

claims.text: if the SVT persists after 1–2 min, give 12 mg rapid IV bolus,
claims.quote: If the first dose does not result in elimination of the supraventricular tachycardia within 1 to 2 minutes, 12 mg should be given as a rapid intravenous bolus.
This 12 mg dose may be repeated a second time if required.
Doses greater than 12 mg are not recommended for adult and pediatric patients.

claims.text: SE: a brief (2–3 s) ♡ standstill can occur;
claims.quote: Adenosine sometimes causes a brief (2- to 3-second) period of cardiac standstill

claims.text: transient or prolonged asystole, sometimes fatal, has been reported.
claims.quote: Transient or prolonged episodes of asystole have been reported with fatal outcomes in some cases.

claims.text: It can cause short-lasting first-, second- or third-degree AV block;
claims.quote: may produce a short lasting first-, second- or third-degree heart block.
Patients who develop high-level block on one dose of adenosine should not be given additional doses.

claims.text: Asthma has worsened after IV adenosine.
claims.quote: Adenosine injection has been administered to a limited number of patients with asthma and mild to moderate exacerbation of their symptoms has been reported.

claims.text: CI: second- or third-degree AV block,
claims.quote: Second- or third-degree A-V block (except in patients with a functioning artificial pacemaker).

claims.text: or sinus node dz (sick sinus syndrome, Sxtomatic brady), unless a functioning pacemaker = in place.
claims.quote: Sinus node disease, such as sick sinus syndrome or symptomatic bradycardia (except in patients with a functioning artificial pacemaker).
should be avoided in patients with bronchoconstriction or bronchospasm (e.g., asthma).

claims.text: Interactions: methylxanthines (caffeine, theophylline) antagonize it, so lrger doses may be needed or it may ⍉work;
claims.quote: In the presence of these methylxanthines, larger doses of adenosine may be required or adenosine may not be effective.

claims.text: dipyridamole potentiates it, so smaller doses may work.
claims.quote: Thus, smaller doses of adenosine may be effective in the presence of dipyridamole.
higher degrees of heart block may be produced in the presence of carbamazepine.

claims.text: Use w caution w digoxin (± verapamil): rare VF has been reported.
claims.quote: adenosine should be used with caution in patients receiving digoxin or digoxin and verapamil in combination.

claims.text: OD: the ½ life = under 10 s, so SE are generally rapidly self-limiting;
claims.quote: The half-life of adenosine injection is less than 10 seconds. Thus, adverse effects are generally rapidly self-limiting.
Treatment of any prolonged adverse effects should be individualized and be directed toward the specific effect.
